rows.gloss: going to the tip of the goddess-circle

items.question: What result comes from meditating on the trident up to the twelve-end-point?
premises: One remembers the trident extending from the root to the twelve-end-point.
One reaches the tip of the goddess-circle and abandons sequential progression.
This meditation produces the state of moving in space.
items.inference: By meditating on the trident to the twelve-end-point and transcending sequence, the practitioner attains khecaratā.
uncertainties: The exact referent of dvādaśānta in this ritual context is assumed from standard Tantric usage.
items.plain_english: Remembering the trident extending from the root up to the twelve-end-point, with its tip forward, and reaching the tip of the circle of goddesses while abandoning sequence, one attains the state of moving in space.

rows.gloss: filling from the root-support to the top of the space at the end of the twelve
by moving and abiding in space
by feeding on the nectar of space

items.question: Why is this power called khecarī in this context?
premises: Khecarī fills the path from the root-support to the top of the space at the end of the twelve.
She is associated with moving and abiding in space.
She is associated with feeding on the nectar of space.
items.inference: The name khecarī is explained by her pervasion of the inner space and her movement, abiding, and nourishment in that space.
uncertainties: dviṣaṭka is taken as referring to the twelvefold endpoint in line with the previous verse.
items.plain_english: This khecarī fills everything from the root-support up to the top of the space at the end of the twelve; she is called khecarī because she moves and abides in space and feeds on the nectar of space.

rows.gloss: from that Śāmbhava trident one should reduce by four finger-widths
and from that also in the Āṇava

items.question: How are the Śākta and Āṇava tridents positioned relative to the Śāmbhava trident?
premises: The Śāmbhava trident is the reference point.
The Śākta trident is reduced by four finger-widths from it.
The Āṇava trident is reduced by four finger-widths from the Śākta.
items.inference: A triad of tridents is established in descending measure from Śāmbhava to Śākta to Āṇava.
items.plain_english: From that Śāmbhava trident one should reduce by four finger-widths for the Śākta, and from that again for the Āṇava; thus that triad of tridents is established.

rows.gloss: one whose self is offered to the higher and higher goddess-circles on that triad of tridents

items.question: What powers belong to one who has offered the self to the goddess-circles on the three tridents?
premises: The practitioner offers the self to the successive goddess-circles on the triad of tridents.
The verse frames the result as a series of rhetorical questions.
Birth, knowledge, and action are all included in the scope of the result.
items.inference: Such a practitioner is presented as having unrestricted power in becoming, knowing, and doing.
items.plain_english: For one whose self is offered to the higher and higher circles of goddesses on that triad of tridents, what is not born, what is not known, or what is not done?

rows.gloss: by options of union, limbs, faces, and being or non-being in the paired mode

items.question: How may each goddess or mantra be worshipped in the lotus?
premises: The worship may focus on each single goddess or each single mantra.
The locus of worship is a lotus.
The form of worship varies by paired-union, limbs, faces, and being or non-being.
items.inference: The rite allows detailed alternative configurations for worshipping each goddess or mantra in the lotus.
uncertainties: yāmalaikyāṅgavaktrādisadasattāvikalpataḥ is compressed and may admit more than one ritual unpacking.
items.plain_english: Alternatively, one should worship each single goddess or each mantra in a lotus, varying the worship according to paired union, limbs, faces, and other options of being or non-being.

rows.gloss: from breath up to the level of space
then through worship-yoga by making it Śiva

items.question: When should the external rite be performed in relation to inner transformation?
premises: One's own consciousness is to be made Śiva from the level of breath up to the level of space.
This inner transformation is accomplished through worship-yoga.
The external rite follows that inner preparation.
items.inference: The external ritual procedure should be performed only after one's consciousness has been inwardly transformed into Śiva.
items.plain_english: In this way, having made one's own consciousness Śiva from the level of breath up to the level of space through the yoga of worship, one should then perform the external rite.

items.question: What role does internal worship play when external worship is treated as primary?
premises: External worship may be pursued for powers and similar aims.
Internal worship serves as purification in that case.
Without that inner purification, the worshipper remains a bound soul.
items.inference: Even when external worship is primary, internal worship is necessary to purify the practitioner.
items.plain_english: When external worship is made primary and is aimed at powers and the like, internal worship is for purification; otherwise the worshipper remains a bound soul.

rows.gloss: turned away from powers and such
for ascent into the inner great worship

items.question: What is the purpose of external worship for one indifferent to powers?
premises: Some practitioners are not oriented toward powers.
They still worship the Lord outwardly.
Their outward worship serves ascent into the inner great worship.
items.inference: For the disinterested practitioner, external worship is fulfilled when it leads to inner great worship.
items.plain_english: But whoever is turned away from powers and the like and worships the Lord outwardly for the sake of rising into the inner great worship, that person is fulfilled by that very means.

rows.gloss: having performed the inner worship and taken up
grain and such with the weapon-mantra
one should throw for the removal of obstacles
having gathered it back toward the Īśāna direction

items.question: What is the sequence for using consecrated grain to remove obstacles?
premises: The inner worship is performed first.
Grain and similar materials are consecrated with the weapon-mantra.
The consecrated material is thrown in the directions and then gathered toward the Īśāna direction.
items.inference: Obstacle removal proceeds by inner worship, mantra consecration, directional dispersal, and retraction toward Īśāna.
items.plain_english: After performing the inner worship, one should take grain and the like consecrated with the weapon-mantra, throw it in the directions to remove obstacles, and then gather it back toward the Īśāna direction.

rows.gloss: common in the doctrine of Triśiras

items.question: Which purificatory acts are treated as common in the Triśiras doctrine?
premises: The verse lists inspection, sprinkling, striking, nourishing, and covering.
These acts are grouped as saṃskāras.
They are said to be common in the doctrine of Triśiras.
items.inference: The Triśiras tradition recognizes a shared set of five purificatory acts.
items.plain_english: Inspection, sprinkling, striking and nourishing, and covering are purifications that are common in the doctrine of Triśiras.

rows.gloss: cow urine, cow dung, curd, milk, and ghee
one should consecrate with the faces
ending with the upper one, together with the six limbs

items.question: How are the five cow products consecrated and used for sprinkling?
premises: The five cow products are cow urine, cow dung, curd, milk, and ghee.
They are consecrated with the faces ending in the upper one and with the six limbs.
Kuśa-water is used for sprinkling.
items.inference: The pañcagavya materials are ritually empowered by mantra and applied through sprinkling with kuśa-water.
items.plain_english: One should consecrate cow urine, cow dung, curd, milk, and ghee with the faces ending in the upper one and with the six limbs, and sprinkle with this kuśa-water.

rows.gloss: one should set down the pañcagavya

items.question: How is the pañcagavya prepared and designated in this rite?
premises: The ground is sprinkled and the remainder is kept for the disciple.
The pañcagavya consists of five cow products.
When these are in kuśa-water, that mixture is called pañcagavya.
items.inference: The rite defines pañcagavya as the five cow products combined in kuśa-water, used for sprinkling and for the disciple.
items.plain_english: One should sprinkle the ground and set aside the remainder of the pañcagavya for the disciple; where the five cow products are in this kuśa-water, that is called pañcagavya.

rows.gloss: has been removed, then the inner

items.question: What kind of impurity does pañcagavya-water remove according to the scripture?
premises: The scripture identifies pañcagavya-water as removing external impurity.
Ordinary impurity must be removed first.
Only after that is the inner impurity addressed.
items.inference: Pañcagavya-water functions at the level of external purification, preparing the way for inner purification.
items.plain_english: In the scripture, pañcagavya-water is said to remove external impurity; for when ordinary impurity has been removed, one may then deal with the inner impurity.

rows.gloss: to burn away one must resort to
extending from earth up to Śiva

items.question: What means are used to burn away inner impurity after external purification?
premises: Inner impurity requires a non-ordinary means.
Mantra and related practices are used for this purpose.
The goddess is remembered in a form ending with phāṭ and extending from earth to Śiva.
items.inference: Inner impurity is removed through non-ordinary mantra practice centered on the goddess who pervades the whole range from earth to Śiva.
uncertainties: phādināntāṃ is taken as indicating a mantra ending in phāṭ.
items.plain_english: To burn away impurity, one must resort to non-ordinary means such as mantra; one should remember the goddess, ending with phāṭ, who extends from earth up to Śiva.

rows.gloss: one should throw in the middle
incense, fragrance, liquor, and so on
one should give in the middle of the worship-ground

items.question: What offerings are placed in the center and what immediate effect do they have?
premises: A handful of flowers is thrown into the middle.
Incense, fragrance, liquor, and similar offerings are given there as well.
These offerings quickly affect the ritual support or body.
items.inference: Central offerings of flowers and other substances rapidly empower the ritual support.
uncertainties: vigraham may refer to a ritual body, image, or support; the translation keeps it general.
items.plain_english: One should throw a handful of flowers into the middle and likewise offer incense, fragrance, liquor, and so on in the center of the worship-ground; by that the support is quickly empowered.

rows.gloss: on the petals beginning with Dharma
on the pericarp of true knowledge

items.question: How is the entire circle of deities ritually established in this support?
premises: The entire deity-circle is conceived as presiding there.
Its locus is described as the stalk of Ananta, the petals beginning with Dharma, and the pericarp of true knowledge.
The verse presents a structured ritual visualization.
items.inference: The whole deity-circle is installed as the presiding presence within a cosmically structured lotus-support.
uncertainties: sadvaidyakarṇike is read as 'pericarp of true knowledge'; the compound is somewhat compressed.
items.plain_english: The entire circle of deities is conceived as presiding there, on the stalk of Ananta, on the petals beginning with Dharma, and on the pericarp of true knowledge.

rows.gloss: Gaṇeśa with fragrance, flowers, and so on

items.question: What is the procedure for worshipping Gaṇeśa to remove obstacles?
premises: Gaṇeśa, associated with Īśāna, is worshipped with fragrance, flowers, and other offerings.
The worship is performed for the calming of obstacles.
After worship, Gaṇeśa is dismissed.
items.inference: Obstacle removal includes a brief installation, worship, and dismissal of Gaṇeśa in the Īśāna-related mode.
uncertainties: ṣaḍutthe is obscure here and may refer to a specific ritual configuration.
items.plain_english: In the sixfold arising, one should worship Gaṇeśa of Īśāna, placed there, with fragrance, flowers, and the like for the calming of obstacles; having worshipped him, one should dismiss him.

rows.gloss: filled with supremely fragrant liquid substances

items.question: What preparation of the jar follows after the missing portion of the text?
premises: The first part of the verse is missing in the transmitted text.
The surviving portion introduces the next step with 'then'.
A jar filled with supremely fragrant liquid substances is prepared.
items.inference: Despite the lacuna, the sequence continues with preparation of a jar filled with fragrant liquids.
uncertainties: The first half of the verse is missing, so the full syntactic context is unknown.
items.plain_english: After the missing portion of the text: then one should take the jar, filled with supremely fragrant liquid substances.

rows.gloss: one should consecrate one hundred times

items.question: How should the jar and water-pot be consecrated if the weapon-worship was not done earlier?
premises: The jar is worshipped and anointed with the root mantra.
It is consecrated one hundred times.
If the weapon-worship was not done earlier, the water-pot is consecrated with the sword-mantra.
items.inference: The rite requires repeated root-mantra consecration of the jar and, conditionally, sword-mantra consecration of the water-pot.
uncertainties: asinā is taken as the weapon or sword-mantra in this ritual context.
items.plain_english: The jar, worshipped and anointed with the root mantra, should be consecrated one hundred times; if the weapon-worship was not done earlier, the water-pot should be consecrated with the sword-mantra.

rows.gloss: together with the vessel placed on the left
taking refuge in the solar direction
one should worship the world-lords together with their weapons

items.question: Where are the jar and the world-lords worshipped in the next stage of the rite?
premises: The jar, together with the vessel on its left, is worshipped in the Īśāna direction.
After that, the practitioner turns to the solar direction.
The world-lords are worshipped there together with their weapons.
items.inference: The ritual proceeds spatially from the Īśāna-direction jar worship to worship of the armed world-lords in the solar direction.
uncertainties: sauradig is taken as the eastern or sun-associated direction.
items.plain_english: One should worship that jar in the Īśāna direction together with the vessel placed on its left; then, taking position in the solar direction, one should worship the world-lords together with their weapons.

rows.gloss: with offerings of fragrance, flowers, and so on according to rule
the disciple holding the sword-vessel in hand

items.question: What does the disciple do after the world-lords have been worshipped?
premises: The world-lords are worshipped with offerings and mantra according to rule.
After that, the disciple takes the sword-vessel in hand.
The disciple pours down a stream.
items.inference: Following mantra-offering worship, the disciple begins the pouring of a ritual stream while holding the sword-vessel.
uncertainties: asikalaśī is interpreted as a vessel associated with the sword or weapon.
items.plain_english: After worshipping them with offerings of fragrance, flowers, and so on according to rule and preceded by mantra, the disciple, holding the sword-vessel in hand, pours down a stream.

rows.gloss: to be followed by the one with the jar in hand

items.question: What command does the guru give while following the disciple with the jar?
premises: The guru follows the disciple while holding the jar.
The guru speaks a direct address to Śakra.
The command concerns calming obstacles in Śakra's own direction.
items.inference: During the pouring rite, the guru enjoins Śakra to pacify obstacles in his directional domain.
items.plain_english: The guru, holding the jar in hand, should follow while saying this: 'O Śakra, by you, in your own direction, obstacles must be calmed.'

rows.gloss: until the end of the rite

items.question: How is the spoken formula adjusted for a three-syllable name associated with Nirṛti?
premises: The guardian must remain attentive until the rite is completed by Śiva's command.
A special case arises with a three-syllable name mostly belonging to Nirṛti.
In that case only one 'bhoḥ' is used.
items.inference: The command remains in force, but its vocative form is metrically or ritually adjusted for a Nirṛti-associated three-syllable name.
uncertainties: The exact grammatical reason for dropping one 'bhoḥ' is not fully explicit in the verse.
items.plain_english: One must remain attentive until the end of the rite, by Śiva's command; but in a three-syllable name mostly belonging to Nirṛti, only a single 'bhoḥ' should be used.

rows.gloss: this mantra is spoken as bound by meter

items.question: Why is one vocative removed and where is the jar placed afterward?
premises: One 'bhoḥ' is removed because the mantra is bound by meter.
After that adjustment, the rite continues.
The jar is placed in the Īśāna direction upon the scattered offerings.
items.inference: The mantra is adjusted for metrical correctness, and the jar is then installed in the Īśāna direction on the scattered offerings.
items.plain_english: One should remove it because this mantra is spoken as bound by meter; then that jar should be placed in the Īśāna direction upon the scattered offerings.
